```sh
kafka quota alter
```

Set or remove client quota values for one entity

Shared options and defaults: [connection profiles, JSON output, logging and help](../../../global-options/).

## Defaults

Only supplied set/unset operations are applied; an empty entity name selects a cluster-default entity.

## Before you run

Changes client limits and may throttle live applications. Save current quota entries; restore them explicitly if the change affects service health.

## Flags

| Flag                                | Description                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--brokers <string>`                | comma-separated broker list, e.g. localhost:9092                            |
| `--entity <key=value> (repeatable)` | an entity type=name to alter, or type= for its cluster default (repeatable) |
| `--set <key=value> (repeatable)`    | a quota key=value to set (repeatable)                                       |
| `--unset <string> (repeatable)`     | a quota key to remove (repeatable)                                          |
| `--dry-run`                         | validate without changing anything                                          |

## Examples

```sh
kafka quota alter --entity user=alice --set producer_byte_rate=1048576 --brokers localhost:9092
kafka quota alter --entity user=alice --entity client-id=orders-producer --unset producer_byte_rate --brokers localhost:9092
```

## Output

Illustrative, abbreviated output. Empty arrays show the result envelope; actual entries, identifiers, optional fields and broker errors depend on the request and cluster.

With `--json`:

```json
{
  "entries": []
}
```

Declared exit codes: `0`, `1`, `2`. See the exit-code reference for meanings.
